title: What Generative Artificial Intelligence Means for Terminological Definitions
venue: 3rd International Conference on Multilingual digital terminology today. Design, representation formats and management systems
extended_summary:
This paper examines how generative artificial intelligence, especially ChatGPT and similar large language model chatbots, is changing the creation and use of terminological definitions. The author argues that these tools can reduce the time and effort required to draft definitions, but also raise concerns about factual errors, hallucinations, bias, plagiarism, and inconsistency across repeated queries.

The paper is primarily a conceptual and position-oriented analysis rather than an empirical study. It discusses AI-assisted terminography, with particular emphasis on post-editing workflows in which the terminologist uses ChatGPT to draft a definition and then verifies, corrects, or refines it. It also outlines prompt strategies, such as specifying contextual and functional constraints, requesting non-redundant term-initial wording, using templates, and asking for multiple definitions when a term is polysemous.

The context is professional terminology work, not education. The paper suggests that ChatGPT can support definition writing by helping analyze existing definitions, extract semantic traits from concordance lines, and refine drafts, especially when combined with corpus tools such as Sketch Engine. The main conclusion is that AI will likely become integrated into terminology workflows, increasing productivity while making human and AI-generated terminological content increasingly difficult to distinguish; however, reliability concerns mean human validation remains essential.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI large language model chatbot for general-purpose conversational text generation and assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a generative AI tool for creating, refining, analyzing, and validating terminological definitions; the paper also includes example prompts and responses from ChatGPT 4 in March 2024.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical paper rather than an empirical evaluation. It discusses possible uses, risks, and workflows for ChatGPT in terminography, but reports no experimental design, sample, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No effect sizes or outcome data are reported, so there is no measurable impact evidence to rate. The paper’s claims are speculative and illustrative rather than empirical.
